key_insight: This paper shows how to turn standard neural networks into discretization-agnostic neural operators that work directly with continuous function data. The result is models that can learn scientific dynamics and generalize more reliably across different simulation resolutions.
problem_solved: Traditional neural networks often depend on a fixed grid or input resolution, which makes them brittle when scientific data are sampled differently. This paper addresses the challenge of building operator-learning models that remain consistent across discretizations and continuous domains.
method: Extend popular neural architectures into function-space formulations suitable for operator learning.
Design the models to be discretization-agnostic so they can consume continuous scientific data rather than only fixed-size arrays.
Enable learning mappings between functions, improving transfer across resolutions in scientific simulations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a principled path to build more generalizable models for physics, climate, fluid dynamics, and other scientific applications. It reduces sensitivity to mesh or grid choice, making learned simulators more robust and practical.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of standard neural networks on fixed grids vs. neural operators on continuous functions

paper_title: Principled approaches for extending neural architectures to function spaces for operator learning
paper_authors: Julius Berner, Miguel Liu-Schiaffini, Jean Kossaifi, Valentin Duruisseaux, Boris Bonev
